items.text: A country's armed forces should be strong enough to defeat any likely enemy, even at great cost.
items.rationale: Reworded 2026-10-31: capacity to defeat any likely enemy, not expeditionary power projection, so territorial-defence hawks also agree; recoded. Was 06, reworded as a design goal rather than a capability. Power-projection hawks hold this. Mirrors mil-02.

items.text: A country is better off with only a small military, even if a stronger neighbour could then overpower it.
items.rationale: Replaces 14, which was too extreme and could be read as militia-republican. Strong minimal-defence view that accepts vulnerability. Mirrors mil-01.

items.text: If a foreign government is slaughtering its own people, other countries should step in with military force to stop it.
items.rationale: Was 03; the condition favours hawks. Slight Internationalist cross-load, partly offset by mil-06.

items.text: If a military mission abroad is causing many civilian deaths, it should be ended, even before its goals are met.
items.rationale: Was 10, toned down to L2 as the review advised; the condition favours doves.

items.text: If a hostile government is close to building nuclear weapons, a military strike to stop it is justified.
items.rationale: Was 02, relabelled conditional. A counter-proliferation first strike, worded as its advocates would put it rather than as a caricature. The condition favours hawks.

items.text: If talks with another country fail, giving up part of what is disputed is better than going to war.
items.rationale: Was 11, narrowed. The condition favours hawks and the answer is strongly dovish. Slight Sovereigntist cross-load, partly offset by mil-03.

items.text: Using armed force abroad to defend a country's vital interests is justified, even when no one has attacked it.
items.rationale: Was 01; 'vital' softened to 'important'. Realists and interventionists. Rough complement of mil-08, deliberately kept out of the quick and standard tiers.

items.text: Military force should be used only to defend against an armed attack.
items.rationale: Was 08. Reworded so it allows collective defence of allies, which removes the Sovereigntist pull. Defensive-only doves.

items.text: If a country has been at peace for decades with no clear enemy, its armed forces should be ready for a major war.
items.rationale: Was 07, now an 'If' item; 'no clear enemy' makes it polar. The condition favours doves. Mirrors mil-10.

items.text: If no neighbour poses a serious military threat, a country's armed forces should be small.
items.rationale: Replaces 12, which the audit found unclear and which loaded on welfare spending. It is now a direct capacity claim. The condition favours doves.

items.text: An attack on a military target can be justified even when it is expected to kill some civilians, if the military gain is large enough.
items.rationale: Proportionality / foreseen collateral harm (split from red line R9, which is about targeting civilians on purpose). Accepting it is the Hawkish pole. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: If a country's ally is attacked but the country itself is not, it should stay out of the fighting.
items.rationale: Alliance commitment (review C11): non-intervention even for allies, the Dovish pole. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.
